title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the paper wants to turn an arbitrary series into a continued fraction. To do that, Euler first converts a continued fraction into a series and then inverts the procedure. Pages 140-141 set out the convergent recursions: A=a, B=Ab+1, C=Bc+A, ... for numerators and 𝔄=1, 𝔅=b, ℭ=𝔅c+𝔄, ... for denominators. They also derive the first difference B/𝔅 − A/𝔄 = 1/(𝔄𝔅).

This page (pp. 142-143):

§5 (cont.) Substituting the recursions gives the classical determinant identity. In modern notation, with convergents p_n/q_n, it reads p_{n}q_{n-1} − p_{n-1}q_{n} = (−1)^{n-1}.
- For III−II, the numerator 𝔅(Bc+A) − B(𝔅c+𝔄) reduces to A𝔅 − B𝔄 = −1, so C/ℭ − B/𝔅 = −1/(𝔅ℭ).
- Likewise D/𝔇 − C/ℭ = +1/(ℭ𝔇).
- In general the successive differences are ±1/(q_{n-1}q_n), with alternating signs.

§6 Telescoping gives each convergent as a partial sum:
B/𝔅 = a + 1/(𝔄𝔅), C/ℭ = a + 1/(𝔄𝔅) − 1/(𝔅ℭ), and so on.

§7 The value s of the infinite continued fraction a + 1/(b + 1/(c + ...)) is the alternating series
s = a + 1/(𝔄𝔅) − 1/(𝔅ℭ) + 1/(ℭ𝔇) − ...
The denominators need only the recursion 𝔄=1, 𝔅=b, ℭ=𝔅c+𝔄, 𝔇=ℭd+𝔅, ...

§8 Since a appears on both sides, it can be dropped:
1/(b + 1/(c + 1/(d + ...))) = 1/(𝔄𝔅) − 1/(𝔅ℭ) + 1/(ℭ𝔇) − ...
The series is finite if the continued fraction terminates.

§9 Announces the converse: given an arbitrary series s = 1/α − 1/β + 1/γ − ..., find an equal continued fraction. This is carried out on the next pages via 𝔄𝔅=α, 𝔅ℭ=β, ..., which leads to Euler's continued-fraction formula for series.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The sign bookkeeping (B𝔄−A𝔅=1, hence numerator A𝔅−B𝔄=−1) is correct. Convergence of the series is implicitly assumed in §7 ('ultima seu infinitesima' fraction gives the true value), without any convergence discussion; this is typical of the period.

ideas.what: Determinant identity for consecutive convergents: p_n q_{n-1} − p_{n-1} q_n = ±1, proved by substituting the three-term recursion
ideas.modern_name: Convergent determinant formula / Wallis–Euler recurrence property
ideas.usually_credited_to: Recursions: Wallis (1655) and Huygens; the identity is classical, also used by Euler 1737
ideas.where_published: E71 De fractionibus continuis dissertatio (1737/1744); Introductio in analysin infinitorum I (1748), ch. 18

ideas.what: Representation of a continued fraction's value as the alternating series Σ(−1)^{n}/(q_{n-1}q_n) of convergent differences
ideas.modern_name: Continued fraction as telescoping series of convergent differences (Euler–Minding type series)

ideas.what: Plan to invert the procedure: an arbitrary alternating series 1/α − 1/β + ... is to be written as a continued fraction
ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (series ↔ continued fraction)
ideas.where_published: Introductio I ch. 18 §§369ff.; E593 itself (Opuscula analytica II, 1785)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard, well-documented textbook material (convergent determinant identity and the series of convergent differences). Euler had already published it in 1737/1748, and it is fully credited to him.
transcription_corrections: In 'IV − III' the expression printed as '𝔈D − C𝔇 = 𝔈(Cd+B) − C(𝔈d+𝔅)' in the scan is ℭD − C𝔇 = ℭ(Cd+B) − C(ℭd+𝔅). The given transcription with ℭ is correct; the image's Fraktur C resembles 𝔈.
Header note: E593 was published in Opuscula analytica II (1785), pp. 138–155; it is not an Opera postuma item.
